name: Duloxetine
summary: An SNRI that treats both mood and chronic pain conditions, including neuropathic pain and fibromyalgia.
mechanism: Balanced inhibition of serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake; analgesic effects are mediated in part via descending pain pathways.

pharmacokinetics.onset: 2–6 weeks for antidepressant effect; pain relief may begin within 1–2 weeks

dosing.adult: 60 mg once daily (depression/GAD); 30 mg/day for the first week in some pain indications

safety.pregnancy: Limited data; no clear major-malformation signal.
safety.lactation: Enters breast milk; limited data — monitor infant.
contraindications: Severe hepatic impairment or end-stage renal disease
warnings: Black-box warning: increased suicidality in children, adolescents, and young adults (≤24 y) early in treatment
Hepatotoxicity — avoid in hepatic impairment and with heavy alcohol use
monitoring: Mood and suicidality early in treatment
safety.overdose: Overdose causes serotonin syndrome and sedation; generally less dangerous than TCAs.

clinicalPearls: CYP1A2 substrate — smoking induces the enzyme and can meaningfully lower duloxetine levels.
One drug covers mood plus neuropathic pain — a strong choice when the two co-occur.
good: Depression or GAD with comorbid neuropathic pain, fibromyalgia, or chronic pain.
bad: Hepatic disease, heavy alcohol use, or uncontrolled narrow-angle glaucoma.
